VAL-SKEL-003.description: Three-lane layout renders correctly at 80x24, 120x40, and 60x20 without cell overlap, orphaned box-drawing characters, or cursor-in-content-area issues. Selection state survives the resize sequence.

renderReady.finding: Three-lane layout (Main/Detail/Evidence) with box-drawing separators between lanes. Lane width math is correct: sepCount columns are subtracted from available width before distributing 40%/35%/25% at >=80 width, and 45%/35%/20% at minimum 60 width. The header uses '┬', body uses '│', footer uses '┴'. Layout correctly collapses Evidence lane to 0 below 60 width.

buildLanedRow.finding: Bug fix confirmed: uses []rune(sepRune) to extract the first separator rune correctly for multi-byte UTF-8 box-drawing characters (│, ┬, ┴). Previously this was likely a byte-indexing bug. The function correctly handles the empty-evidence two-lane case (main + detail only) and pads to exactly the target width.

padString.finding: Bug fix confirmed: uses gotui.RuneWidth (display width) instead of byte count for correct truncation of CJK and wide Unicode characters. Previous version had an off-by-one error with multi-byte characters because it used len([]byte(s)) instead of rune-based display width. The fix uses iteration over runes accumulating gotui.RuneWidth(r) and truncates by rune index.

UpdateSize.finding: Does NOT mutate selectedIndex or agents on resize. Only changes width, height, and tooSmall flag. ClampSelection is called exclusively via SetAgents/SetStubAgents, not via UpdateSize. This guarantees selection survives resize.

clampSelectionLocked.finding: Correctly clamps to [0, n-1] range, handles empty and out-of-bounds cases.

navigation_methods.finding: NavigateDown increments selectedIndex modulo n (wraps). NavigateUp decrements with wrap. Both hold c.mu. ClampSelection calls clampSelectionLocked. All navigation is mutex-safe.

tests: TestThreeLanes_WithAgents_ResizeSequence — with stub agents + selection across resize
TestThreeLanes_NavigationThenResize — NavigateDown then resize preserves index
TestThreeLanes_CursorNotInContentArea — cursor in footer or hidden at 80/120/60
assertion_helpers: assertNoOverlap — checks no content beyond terminal width
assertNoOrphanedBoxDrawing — finds separator cols, verifies │ in ≥30% of body rows
findSeparatorColumns — heuristic: column with │ in ≥30% of body rows is a separator
assertFooterPresent — checks ESC+quit keybinds in last row
assertVerticalSeparators — expects ≥2 separator columns at ≥80 width
test_coverage.assessment: COMPREHENSIVE — covers all four VAL-SKEL-003 criteria plus navigation and clamping edge cases

non_blocking_suggestions.description: The assertNoOrphanedBoxDrawing helper uses a heuristic threshold of 30% of body rows to identify separator columns. This is reasonable but could produce false negatives at very tall terminals (e.g., 200 rows). Consider increasing the threshold or adding an explicit separator-column-location verification based on lane math instead of frequency analysis.
non_blocking_suggestions.non_blocking_reason: Current threshold is sufficient for all tested sizes (24, 40, 20). The heuristic works correctly because box-drawing characters are high-frequency within their lane boundary.

non_blocking_suggestions.description: The centerInWidth function uses len(s) for width comparison instead of rune-based display width. This means CJK characters in centered labels could be off-center. This is a pre-existing issue in centerInWidth (not introduced by this feature) but worth fixing in a follow-up layout.go extraction refactor.
non_blocking_suggestions.non_blocking_reason: centerInWidth is used only for empty-state guidance text ('No agents running.', 'Select an agent.') which are pure ASCII. No impact in current usage.

architectural_notes.detail: cockpit.go defines both StubAgent (deprecated) and AgentInventoryItem (current). SetStubAgents converts to AgentInventoryItem internally. This dual type is intentional per the walking-skeleton approach but the deprecated path should be removed in M4.

The evidence drawer is rendered by compositing into a gotui.Buffer then writing as text into an overlay element. This is a reasonable skeleton approach but the buffer-to-text round-trip loses style information. For the production Detail lane, the drawer should render as a proper overlay component using z-ordering, not string compositing.

UpdateSize holds the mutex but only sets width/height/tooSmall/phase. It does not call clampSelectionLocked or mutate agents/selectedIndex. Selection state is preserved across resize solely because UpdateSize is idempotent with respect to state. This design choice is correct.

criterion_1_no_overlapping_cells.mechanism: padString explicitly pads to 'width' characters. buildLanedRow concatenates lanes and passes the total width. renderReady computes available width = width - sepCount before distributing lane widths. The available width minus all lane content is exactly the padding needed.

criterion_2_no_orphaned_box_drawing.code_path: cockpit.go:renderReady builds header with '┬', body with '│', footer with '┴'
criterion_2_no_orphaned_box_drawing.mechanism: Each body row uses the same separator rune. Separators are consistent. The '│' in body rows runs from header to footer without breaks for unselected rows. Selected rows may overwrite with selection highlight, which the test tolerance accounts for.

criterion_3_cursor_not_in_content_area.code_path: go-tui renders elements with no explicit cursor positioning in the content area
criterion_3_cursor_not_in_content_area.mechanism: MockTerminal shows cursor either hidden or in the footer area (last row, y=height-1). The cockpit uses gotui.Element hierarchy without manual cursor placement, so the cursor defaults to the PTY origin. Test verifies this.

criterion_4_selection_survives_resize_se.code_path: cockpit.go:UpdateSize does not mutate selectedIndex; clampSelectionLocked only called from SetAgents/SetStubAgents
criterion_4_selection_survives_resize_se.mechanism: Resize only updates dimensions. selectedIndex is never modified by resize events. Tests verify NavigateDown → UpdateSize → SelectedIndex() == 1 and full resize sequence 80→120→60→80.
